original_question: (Manes, 2008, [157]). A Q-rational periodic point of a map of the form bx + cx−1 with b, c ∈ Q∗ has period 1, 2, or 4. Further,  sup # PrePer bx + cx−1 , P1 (Q) = 12. b,c∈Q∗.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Conjecture 4.6 (Manes, 2008), in the discussion of uniform boundedness for rational preperiodic points in the odd degree-2 family f(x)=bx+c/x.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the exact target almost verbatim: it identifies the family of maps f(x)=bx+cx^{-1} with b,c in Q^×, states the claimed restriction on Q-rational periodic-point periods (1, 2, or 4), and includes the extremal statement that the maximum possible number of Q-rational preperiodic points is 12.
missing_details: It should say explicitly that the map is the degree-2 rational self-map f_{b,c}: P^1 -> P^1 defined over Q, given in affine coordinate by f_{b,c}(x)=bx+c/x=(bx^2+c)/x.
The ambient set for periodic and preperiodic points should be specified as P^1(Q), not just Q.
Q^× should be expanded as the set of nonzero rational numbers.
The phrase "has period 1, 2, or 4" should be made explicit as "has exact period 1, 2, or 4" for a Q-rational periodic point P in P^1(Q).
PrePer(f_{b,c}, P^1(Q)) should be defined as the set of Q-rational preperiodic points, using the paper’s Definition 2.1.
The supremum should be written with its quantifiers and parameter range explicitly: over all pairs (b,c) in (Q^×)^2.
To be fully stand-alone, the statement should clarify that the equality to 12 asserts both an upper bound and that it is attained for some maps in the family.

The nearby context notes that these are exactly the degree-2 rational maps satisfying f(-x)=-f(x), and that geometrically the family is 1-dimensional up to twisting by c modulo squares; this is contextual information that explains the scope, even though it is not part of the conjecture itself.
refined_question: Let f_{b,c}: P^1 -> P^1 be the degree-2 rational map defined over Q by f_{b,c}(x)=bx+c/x=(bx^2+c)/x, where b,c ∈ Q^×. Is it true that every Q-rational periodic point P ∈ P^1(Q) of f_{b,c} has exact period 1, 2, or 4, and that the largest possible number of Q-rational preperiodic points in this family is exactly 12; that is, does one have sup_{b,c∈Q^×} #PrePer(f_{b,c}, P^1(Q)) = 12?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Conjecture 4.6, which it reproduces nearly word-for-word. The surrounding context in Section 4 identifies the family as the degree-2 rational maps on P^1 with the odd symmetry f(-x)=-f(x), while Definition 2.1 supplies the precise meanings of periodic, exact period, and preperiodic. The section-opening discussion also fixes that rational functions are viewed as self-maps of P^1(K). Footnote 3 adds an important but secondary clarification: although written with two parameters b and c, this is geometrically a 1-dimensional family over an algebraically closed field, with c acting as a twist parameter modulo squares. Because the paper states the conjecture over Q and with explicit parameters b,c∈Q^×, the refined question keeps that exact arithmetic formulation and does not broaden it to the larger quadratic-map conjecture in Conjecture 4.7.
